subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: 4D Printing: Objects That Change Shape Over Time
description: One-minute skill: 4D Printing: Objects That Change Shape Over Time.

hook.text: 4D printing adds time as the fourth dimension. Objects are printed from materials that change shape when exposed to heat or water.

buildup.text: Shape-memory polymers remember their original form. Deform them, apply heat, and they snap back to their designed shape.

discovery.text: MIT's Self-Assembly Lab prints flat sheets that fold into 3D structures when immersed in water. No motors or electronics needed.

twist.text: Imagine water pipes that expand with flow, or stents that unfold inside arteries. Applications span medicine and construction.

climax.text: 4D printing is still in its infancy. Material reliability and cost remain barriers. But programmable matter is closer than ever.

punchline.text: Print it flat. Add water. Watch it fold itself. The fourth dimension is time.

quiz.question: What makes 4D printing different from 3D printing?
options: 4D printers can print four materials simultaneously instead of one
4D-printed objects change shape over time when exposed to stimuli like heat or water
4D printing uses four print heads operating at different angles
